clues: These first evolved roughly 40 to 50 million years before true mammals, developing alongside high metabolic rates and warm-bloodedness.
These naturally swell and shrink in alternating shifts throughout the day, typically switching every 2.5 hours. Lying down increases blood flow and can increase swelling.

Early doctors viewed these as culprits behind asthma, headaches, and chronic congestion. This led to aggressive, destructive full-scale removal that frequently caused severe complications like empty nose syndrome. We now recognize them as vital organs that heat, humidify, and filter air.

This drug was initially isolated by Abbott Laboratories in the 1970-80s but they decided to out-license it to PathoGenesis in the 90s. Chiron Corp then acquired PathoGenesis in 2000 but wasn't interested in this medication and sold the licensing rights to a startup, Optimer Pharmaceuticals. Just as Optimer gained FDA approval in 2011, a major compliance scandal emerged and the company imploded. Optimer was bought by Cubist which was then bought by Merck and finally reached the market.

When Abbott Laboratories was developing the drug in the 1980s, the entire pharmaceutical industry was obsessed with finding a cure for MRSA. This drug was fantastic at killing MRSA in test tubes but animal tesing showed that the drug was not absorbed when swallowed.

Because it is barely absorbed, it acts locally in the GI tract and has a narrow spectrum of action. It binds to bacterial RNA polymerase and halts transcription but also uniquely inhibits spore production and toxin formation, lowering the chance of recurrent infection.
Hippocrates coined the name of this condition from the Greek word ischios, meaning hip. He thought that symptoms were caused by localized disease or subluxation of the hip joint

The Italian anatomist, Domenico Contugno, proved that this condition is an affliction of the nerve rather than the hip joint. For generations, the condition was widely called Cotugno’s disease. Cotugno also famously discovered cerebrospinal fluid
In 1864, Ernest Lasègue linked low back trouble with leg pain and described the physical mechanics of lifting a straight leg to test for this condition.

In the 1930s, white medical leaders claimed Black people were immune to this disease, leaving many Black children undiagnosed or denied treatment. In 1941, Tuskegee opened the only facility in the US specifically built to treat Black patients with this condition and helped train the next generation of Black orthopedic specialists
Egyptian artwork and skeletal remains show classic signs of limb deformities from this disease dating back over 3,300 years

A 1954 evaluation of a vaccine for this disease involved 1.4 million schoolchildren and was one of the first applications of the double-blind trial method. Salk famously chose not to seek a patent or personal profit to ensure it could be distributed globally as fast as possible saying 'there is no patent. Could you patent the sun?'
The causal abnormal protein clumps were discovered in 1912 on autopsy although the first official diagnostic consensus criteria of this disease was not published until 1996

Robin Williams had this disease which was diagnosed on autopsy. Years before his death, his sleep patterns changed dramatically and experienced worsened depression and anxiety. He also developed a tremor of his left hand and stiffness

Parkinson's disease is also driven by the same abnormal clumping of alpha-synuclein proteins. However, this disease primarily starts with cognitive and perceptual symptoms such as detailed visual hallucinations with movement symptoms appearing within a year
